learn.hook: 2 samosas and 3 jalebis cost ₹110. How much is one samosa? There isn't just one answer, until you get more clues!
points: A linear equation in two variables can be written as ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero.
A solution is an ordered pair (x, y) that makes the equation true. Example: (2, 3) is a solution of 2x + y = 7 because 4 + 3 = 7.
A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions: choose any x, then work out y.
To check a pair, substitute both values and see whether the two sides are equal.
An equation like y = 3 can be written in two variables as 0·x + 1·y − 3 = 0.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers mixing two kinds of sweets in a ₹500 box face a two-variable equation: many different mixes give the same total.

games.title: Is it a solution of 2x + y = 7?

items.text: x + y = 10. If x = 4, then y = ___
x − y = 5. If y = 2, then x = ___
A linear equation in two variables has ___ solutions

quiz.q: Which ordered pair is a solution of 2x + y = 7?
quiz.mistake: Swaps x and y in the ordered pair

quiz.q: A pen costs ₹x and a notebook costs ₹y. 2 pens and 3 notebooks cost ₹110. Which equation shows this?
quiz.explain: Cost of 2 pens = 2x and of 3 notebooks = 3y. Together: 2x + 3y = 110.
quiz.mistake: Attaches the numbers to the wrong items

quiz.q: If (k, 2) is a solution of 3x − 2y = 8, what is k?
quiz.explain: Substitute x = k, y = 2: 3k − 4 = 8, so 3k = 12 and k = 4.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 4 instead of adding it, getting 4/3

quiz.q: How many solutions does x + y = 10 have?
quiz.explain: For every value of x there is a matching y = 10 − x, such as (1, 9), (2.5, 7.5), (−3, 13), and so on.
quiz.mistake: Counts only whole-number solutions, or treats it like a one-variable equation

quiz.q: Write 4x − 5y + 6 = 0 in the form ax + by + c = 0. What is b?
quiz.explain: Compare term by term: a = 4, b = −5, c = 6. The sign belongs to the coefficient.
quiz.mistake: Drops the minus sign in front of 5y

quiz.q: For x + 2y = 12, find y when x = 4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 2, giving y = 8

quiz.q: How can y = 3 be written as a linear equation in two variables?
quiz.explain: The coefficient of x is 0, so x can take any value while y stays 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an equation without x cannot have two variables

quiz.q: A box holds 60 sweets: x laddoos and y pedas. Which equation describes the box?
quiz.explain: The numbers of laddoos and pedas together make 60.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the two amounts instead of adding them

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "For x + y = 5, my friend says the answer is (2, 3) and I say (1, 4). Who is right?"
teach.praise: You are both right! Put each pair in and the sum is 5. A two-variable equation has infinitely many solutions. Happy chirps!
teach.nudge: What happens when you put (2, 3) and (1, 4) into x + y? Can an equation like this have more than one answer?

topics.title: Standard form, scaling and solutions in every quadrant

learn.hook: x/2 + y/3 = 1 and 3x + 2y = 6 look different, but they are the very same line!
points: To write an equation in standard form ax + by + c = 0, move every term to one side and clear fractions or decimals by multiplying by a suitable number.
Example: x/2 + y/3 = 1 → multiply by 6: 3x + 2y = 6 → 3x + 2y − 6 = 0, so a = 3, b = 2, c = −6.
Check that an equation really matches a situation by testing a simple case: if a pen costs ₹10 and a pencil ₹5, 'x pens and y pencils cost ₹80' is 10x + 5y = 80, not 10x + 5y = 80xy.
Multiplying an equation by any non-zero k gives the same solutions (the same line): 2x + y = 5 and 6x + 3y = 15 are equivalent.
Solutions can be in any quadrant: for x − y = 2, (5, 3) is in Quadrant I, (−1, −3) in III, and (1, −1) in IV.

example.q: Write 0.3x − 0.2y = 1.5 in standard form with integer coefficients.

learn.reallife: Mobile plans like '₹2 per call and ₹1 per SMS, total bill ₹150' are linear equations in two variables.

items.text: (−2, −5) for x − y = 3 lies in Quadrant ___

games.title: Same solutions?
items: x + y = 4 and 3x + 3y = 12 have the same solutions.
The second is 3 times the first.
x + y = 4 and x + y = 8 have the same solutions.
Only the right side changed, so the lines are parallel and share no solution.
Multiplying by 0 keeps the same solutions.
x − y = 2 has a solution in Quadrant IV.
0.5x + y = 2 is the same as x + 2y = 4.

quiz.q: Write 2y = 5 − 3x in the form ax + by + c = 0. What is c?
quiz.mistake: Keeps 5 on the wrong side without changing its sign

quiz.q: Write x/3 − y/4 = 2 in standard form with integers. What is b?
quiz.explain: Multiply by 12: 4x − 3y = 24, so 4x − 3y − 24 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Uses the denominator as the coefficient

quiz.q: Which equation has exactly the same solutions as 3x − y = 4?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only some terms

quiz.q: A shop sells chai at ₹15 and samosas at ₹10. Riya buys x chai and y samosas for ₹95. Which equation is correct?
quiz.explain: Cost of chai 15x plus cost of samosas 10y.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the prices

quiz.q: Which solution of x + y = 1 lies in Quadrant II?
quiz.explain: x negative, y positive, and −3 + 4 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Picks a point that is not a solution or is in the wrong quadrant

quiz.q: Is (−2, −7) a solution of 3x − y = 1?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that subtracting −7 adds 7

quiz.q: Why can't we multiply an equation by 0 to get an equivalent one?
options: It becomes 0 = 0, true for every pair
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 0 destroys the information in the equation.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 0 behaves like any other number

quiz.q: A student models '3 kg of rice and 2 kg of dal cost ₹400' as 3x + 2y = 400 with x = price of dal. What is wrong?
options: x should be the price of rice per kg, since it is multiplied by 3 kg of rice
quiz.explain: Each coefficient must go with the matching item.
quiz.mistake: Does not check what each variable stands for

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Why do 2x + y = 5 and 4x + 2y = 10 give the same line?"
teach.praise: Right! One is just 2 times the other, so every solution of one solves the other!
teach.nudge: How is the second equation made from the first? Does that change which pairs work?

learn.hook: Plot every solution of x + y = 5 and they line up perfectly, like students at assembly. One equation, one straight line!
points: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line. Every point on the line is a solution, and every solution is a point on the line.
To draw it, find two or three solutions, plot them and join them with a ruler.
x-intercept: put y = 0. y-intercept: put x = 0. These two points are often the easiest to plot.
x = a is a vertical line through (a, 0); y = b is a horizontal line through (0, b).
y = mx (with no constant term) always passes through the origin (0, 0).

steps: Plot the three points and join them: one straight line

learn.reallife: A taxi fare chart (fare against distance) or a mobile recharge plan (cost against data) shows up as a straight-line graph.

games.title: Line logic
items: Every point on the graph of 2x + y = 6 is a solution of the equation
The line is made of exactly the solutions.
The graph of x = 5 is a horizontal line
x stays 5 while y changes, so the line is vertical.
The point (2, 1) lies on x + y = 4
Two points are enough to draw the graph of a linear equation
Exactly one straight line passes through two points.

quiz.q: What does the graph of x = 4 look like?
quiz.explain: Every point has x = 4 and any y, so the points form a vertical line crossing the x-axis at (4, 0).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up vertical and horizontal lines

quiz.q: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 cut the x-axis?
quiz.explain: On the x-axis y = 0, so 2x = 12 and x = 6. The point is (6, 0).
quiz.mistake: Puts x = 0 instead of y = 0, which gives the y-axis point

quiz.q: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 cut the y-axis?
quiz.explain: On the y-axis x = 0, so 3y = 12 and y = 4. The point is (0, 4).
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide 12 by the coefficient of y

quiz.q: Which line passes through the origin?
quiz.explain: Put x = 0 in y = 5x: y = 0, so (0, 0) is on the line. The others do not contain (0, 0).
quiz.mistake: Thinks every line passes through the origin

quiz.q: The point (2, k) lies on the line y = 3x − 1. What is k?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract 1, or adds it

quiz.q: What does the graph of y = −2 look like?
options: A vertical line left of the y-axis
A horizontal line 2 units below the x-axis
A horizontal line 2 units above the x-axis
quiz.explain: Every point has y = −2, so the line is horizontal and lies 2 units below the x-axis.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the minus sign

quiz.q: Where do the lines x = 3 and y = −1 meet?
quiz.explain: The meeting point must have x = 3 and y = −1, so it is (3, −1).
quiz.mistake: Writes the coordinates in the wrong order

quiz.q: The line x + y = 6 makes a triangle with the two axes. What is the area of this triangle?
quiz.explain: The line meets the axes at (6, 0) and (0, 6). The triangle has base 6 and height 6, so area = ½ × 6 × 6 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ½ in the triangle formula

teach.ask: Gappu has graph paper: "How do I draw the graph of x + y = 4? Do I need lots of points?"
teach.praise: Find two or three solutions like (0, 4), (4, 0) and (2, 2), plot them, and join them with a ruler into a straight line!
teach.nudge: Which pairs (x, y) make x + y = 4 true? What do you do once they are plotted?

learn.hook: A wheelchair ramp must rise only 1 cm for every 12 cm along. That 1 : 12 is its slope!
points: Slope (gradient) measures how steep a line is: slope = rise ÷ run = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁).
On a straight line, the slope is the same whichever two points you use.
Positive slope rises from left to right; negative slope falls; a horizontal line has slope 0; a vertical line has undefined slope (the run is 0).
Real life: ramps, ghats, ski slopes. A wheelchair ramp is recommended to have slope at most 1 : 12, so a 60 cm rise needs at least 7.2 m of run.
Using slope and one point: if the slope is 3 and the line passes through (1, 2), then the point with x = 4 has y = 2 + 3 × 3 = 11.

example.q: A line through (2, 5) has slope −2. Find y when x = 6.

learn.reallife: Government buildings in India add ramps with gentle slopes so that wheelchair users can enter.

quiz.q: Find the slope of the line through (−3, 1) and (5, 5).
quiz.explain: Rise 4, run 8.
quiz.mistake: Divides run by rise

quiz.q: What is the slope of the line through (4, −2) and (4, 7)?
quiz.explain: Run = 4 − 4 = 0, and we cannot divide by 0. The line is vertical.
quiz.mistake: Thinks vertical lines have slope 0

quiz.q: What is the slope of the line y = 6?
quiz.explain: It is horizontal: no rise.
quiz.mistake: Confuses with a vertical line

quiz.q: A ramp must have slope at most 1/12. How long (horizontally) must it be to rise 90 cm?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 12

quiz.q: A ghat road rises 150 m over a horizontal distance of 2 km. What is its slope?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change km to m

quiz.q: A line has slope 4 and passes through (1, 3). What is y when x = 3?
quiz.explain: Run 2, rise 8: 3 + 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds the slope only once

quiz.q: A line falls 3 units for every 5 units it goes right. What is its slope?
quiz.explain: Falling means negative: −3 ÷ 5.
quiz.mistake: Drops the sign

quiz.q: Points A(1, 2), B(3, 6), C(6, 12): is the slope AB the same as BC?
options: Yes, both are 2, so A, B, C lie on one line
quiz.mistake: Uses rise only

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I measure how steep a line is?"
teach.praise: Great! Slope = rise ÷ run between any two points!
teach.nudge: What do you compare between two points? What do you divide by what?

learn.hook: Rewrite 2x + 3y = 6 as y = −(2/3)x + 2 and you can read the slope and where it hits the y-axis at a glance!
points: Slope-intercept form: y = mx + d, where m is the slope and d is the y-intercept (the line meets the y-axis at (0, d)).
From ax + by + c = 0 with b ≠ 0: y = −(a/b)x − c/b. So m = −a/b and d = −c/b.
Two different lines with the same slope are parallel: y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 4.
Applications: a tank filling at 3 litres per minute holds y = 3x after x minutes (slope 3, intercept 0); Fahrenheit and Celsius are linked by F = (9/5)C + 32 (slope 9/5, intercept 32).

example.q: Find the slope and y-intercept of 4x − 2y + 6 = 0.

learn.reallife: An auto fare chart 'base ₹30 plus ₹15 per km' is y = 15x + 30: slope 15, intercept 30.

quiz.q: What is the slope of 3x + 4y − 12 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the minus sign in −a/b

quiz.q: What is the y-intercept of 3x + 4y − 12 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Uses c directly

quiz.q: Which line is parallel to y = 5x − 2?
quiz.explain: 10x − 2y = 3 gives y = 5x − 1.5: slope 5.
quiz.mistake: Compares intercepts instead of slopes

quiz.q: A tank fills at 3 litres per minute starting empty. Which equation gives the litres y after x minutes?
quiz.explain: Slope 3, intercept 0.
quiz.mistake: Treats the rate as an intercept

quiz.q: Using F = (9/5)C + 32, what is the slope and what does it mean?
quiz.explain: The slope is the change in F per unit change in C.
quiz.mistake: Takes the intercept as the slope

quiz.q: Write y = (2/3)x − 4 in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integers. Which is correct?
quiz.explain: Multiply by 3: 3y = 2x − 12, so 2x − 3y − 12 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the constant

quiz.q: Lines y = mx + 4 and y = −3x + 1 are parallel. What is m?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
quiz.mistake: Matches the intercept

quiz.q: A mobile plan charges ₹99 fixed plus ₹10 per GB. In y = mx + d, what are m and d?
quiz.explain: The rate is the slope and the fixed charge is the intercept.
quiz.mistake: Swaps rate and fixed charge

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I find the slope from 2x + 3y = 6?"
teach.praise: Super! Make y the subject: y = −(2/3)x + 2, so the slope is −2/3!
teach.nudge: What should you make y equal to? Which number in front of x is the slope?

learn.hook: One clue gives infinitely many answers. Add a second clue and, usually, just one answer is left. Two lines, one meeting point!
points: Two linear equations in the same two variables form a pair. A solution of the pair must satisfy both equations.
Graphically, the solution is the point where the two lines meet.
Lines that cross give exactly one solution. Parallel lines give no solution. Lines that lie on top of each other (the same line) give infinitely many solutions.
Substitution method: make one variable the subject in one equation and put it into the other.
Elimination method: add or subtract the equations (after multiplying if needed) to remove one variable.

example.q: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 2.
steps: Put x = 6 in x + y = 10: y = 4

learn.reallife: Comparing two mobile plans, or finding prices from two shopping bills, is solving a pair of linear equations.

items.q: x + y = 8, x − y = 2. Find x.
x + y = 8, x − y = 2. Find y.

quiz.q: Solve x + y = 12 and x − y = 4.
quiz.explain: Adding gives 2x = 16, so x = 8; then y = 12 − 8 = 4. Check: 8 − 4 = 4 ✓.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the values of x and y

quiz.q: 2 pens and 1 notebook cost ₹50. 1 pen and 1 notebook cost ₹35. What is the cost of one pen?
quiz.explain: Subtract the second bill from the first: the extra pen costs 50 − 35 = ₹15.
quiz.mistake: Gives the notebook's price (₹20) instead of the pen's

quiz.q: How many solutions does the pair y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 have?
quiz.explain: Both lines have slope 2 but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every pair of lines must cross somewhere

quiz.q: How many solutions does the pair x + 2y = 4 and 2x + 4y = 8 have?
quiz.explain: The second equation is just the first multiplied by 2, so both describe the same line. Every point on it is a solution.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different-looking equations must be different lines

quiz.q: Solve y = 3x and x + y = 20. What is y?
quiz.explain: Substitute y = 3x: x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20, x = 5 and y = 15.
quiz.mistake: Gives the value of x (5) instead of y

quiz.q: Kabir is 4 years older than Aisha. The sum of their ages is 30. How old is Aisha?
quiz.explain: Let Aisha be a and Kabir k: k = a + 4 and a + k = 30. So 2a + 4 = 30, a = 13 and Kabir is 17.
quiz.mistake: Gives Kabir's age (17) or just halves 30

quiz.q: On a graph, how do you read off the solution of a pair of linear equations?
options: Where each line cuts the y-axis
The point where the two lines meet
Where each line cuts the x-axis
quiz.explain: Only the meeting point lies on both lines, so only it satisfies both equations.
quiz.mistake: Reads the intercepts of one line instead of the common point

quiz.q: At a zoo, adult tickets cost ₹60 and child tickets ₹40. A group buys 10 tickets for ₹480. How many adult tickets did they buy?
quiz.explain: Let a adults and c children: a + c = 10 and 60a + 40c = 480. Then 60a + 40(10 − a) = 480, so 20a = 80 and a = 4.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of child tickets (6)

teach.ask: Gappu draws two lines on a graph: "Where is the answer to both equations together?"
teach.praise: The answer is where the two lines meet, because that point is on both. Parallel lines never meet, so then there is no solution. Super!
teach.nudge: Which point is on both lines at once? And what if the lines never meet?

topics.title: Shape puzzles and the comparison method

learn.hook: Two apples and a banana weigh 500 g; one apple and a banana weigh 350 g. Take one picture from the other and an apple pops out!
points: Shape-value puzzles: pictures like 🍎🍎🍌 = 500 and 🍎🍌 = 350 are pairs of equations in disguise. Comparing them shows one 🍎 = 150, then 🍌 = 200.
Comparison method: make the same variable the subject in both equations, then set the two expressions equal.
Example: y = 2x + 1 and y = 7 − x give 2x + 1 = 7 − x, so 3x = 6, x = 2 and y = 5.
Always check the solution in both original equations.

example.q: Solve by comparison: x + y = 9 and x − y = 3.
steps: From both: y = 9 − x and y = x − 3

learn.reallife: Kids' puzzles on social media like 'burger + burger + fries = 30' are simultaneous equations in disguise.

games.title: Comparison method for y = 3x − 2 and y = x + 4

quiz.q: Two laddoos and one barfi cost ₹50. One laddoo and one barfi cost ₹35. What does one laddoo cost?
quiz.explain: Taking away the second order from the first leaves one laddoo: 50 − 35.
quiz.mistake: Divides 50 by 2

quiz.q: Using that laddoo price, what does one barfi cost?
quiz.mistake: Uses the first equation wrongly

quiz.q: Solve by comparison: y = 4x − 3 and y = 2x + 5. What is x?
quiz.explain: 4x − 3 = 2x + 5 gives 2x = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds the expressions instead of equating them

quiz.q: For the pair above, what is y?
quiz.mistake: Substitutes into a wrong equation

quiz.q: In the comparison method, what must you do first?
options: Make the same variable the subject of both equations
quiz.explain: Then the two expressions can be set equal.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with elimination

quiz.q: A puzzle: 🍎 + 🍎 + 🍎 = 30 and 🍎 + 🍌 = 16. What is 🍌?
quiz.mistake: Stops after finding 🍎

quiz.q: Solve by comparison: x = 2y + 1 and x = 5y − 8. What is y?
quiz.explain: 2y + 1 = 5y − 8 gives 9 = 3y.
quiz.mistake: Sets the wrong sides equal

quiz.q: Why should you check your answer in BOTH equations?
options: A solution of the pair must satisfy both
quiz.explain: A slip in one step may give a pair that fits only one equation.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one equation

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How does the comparison method work?"
teach.praise: Wonderful! Make the same variable the subject in both, set them equal, solve and check!
teach.nudge: What should both equations look like before comparing? What do you do next?

topics.title: How many solutions? The ratio test

learn.hook: Without solving, can you tell if two lines cross, never meet, or are the same line? Compare the coefficient ratios!
points: For a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0:
If a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the lines cross: exactly one solution.
If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, the lines are the same (coincident): infinitely many solutions. While solving, you get 0 = 0.
If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the lines are parallel: no solution. While solving, you get a false statement like 0 = 5.

To build a second equation for 2x + 3y = 6: for crossing lines change the ratio of x and y (x − y = 1); for parallel lines keep 2 : 3 but change the constant (4x + 6y = 5); for the same line multiply everything (4x + 6y = 12).

example.q: Decide the number of solutions of 3x − 2y = 5 and 6x − 4y = 9.

learn.reallife: Two trains on parallel tracks never meet; two roads that cross meet at exactly one junction.

items.text: Solving parallel lines gives a statement like ___

quiz.q: How many solutions does the pair 2x + y = 7 and 4x + 2y = 14 have?
quiz.explain: All three ratios equal 1/2: the same line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every pair has one solution

quiz.q: How many solutions does x − 3y = 2 and 2x − 6y = 7 have?
quiz.explain: 1/2 = −3/−6 = 1/2, but 2/7 ≠ 1/2: parallel lines.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the x-ratio

quiz.q: How many solutions does 3x + 2y = 8 and x − y = 1 have?
quiz.explain: 3/1 ≠ 2/(−1), so the lines cross.
quiz.mistake: Thinks different-looking equations must be parallel

quiz.q: While solving a pair, Riya ends up with 0 = 0. What does this mean?
options: The equations describe the same line: infinitely many solutions
quiz.explain: 0 = 0 is always true, so every solution of one is a solution of the other.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 0 = 0 means x = y = 0

quiz.q: While solving a pair, Kabir gets 0 = 6. What does this mean?
options: The lines are parallel: no solution
quiz.explain: A false statement means no pair can satisfy both.
quiz.mistake: Reads it as a value of x

quiz.q: For what value of k are kx + 6y = 4 and 2x + 3y = 5 parallel?
quiz.mistake: Matches the constants

quiz.q: Which equation, paired with 2x − 5y = 3, gives coincident lines?
quiz.mistake: Scales only the left-hand side

quiz.q: Which equation, paired with x + 4y = 8, gives lines that cross at one point?
quiz.explain: 1/2 ≠ 4/(−1), so they intersect.
quiz.mistake: Picks a scaled or parallel equation

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How can I tell if two lines are parallel without drawing them?"
teach.praise: Brilliant! Equal x- and y-ratios but a different constant ratio means parallel!
teach.nudge: Which ratios do you compare? What must be different for parallel lines?

learn.hook: Ages, coins, incomes, ticket prices: two clues give two equations, and two equations crack the case!
points: Name the two unknowns clearly (for example x = price of a pen, y = price of a pencil).
Turn each clue into one equation, then solve the pair by substitution, elimination or comparison.
Two-digit numbers: 10t + u; reversing gives 10u + t. Fractions: write as x/y and turn each clue into an equation.
Income and expenditure in a ratio: incomes 3k and 4k; savings = income − expenditure.
Check the answer against the story: ages must be positive, coins must be whole numbers.

example.q: Find a fraction x/y that becomes 1/2 when 1 is added to its numerator, and 1/3 when 1 is subtracted from its denominator.

learn.reallife: Planning a school picnic budget with buses and vans of different capacities is a two-variable problem.

games.title: Solve a word problem
items: Write one equation for each clue
Check the answer in the story

items.q: Ages: A + B = 40, A − B = 6: B
Digits sum 9, number − reverse = 27: tens digit

quiz.q: The sum of two numbers is 45 and their difference is 13. What is the larger number?
quiz.explain: x + y = 45, x − y = 13: add to get 2x = 58.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to halve

quiz.q: Five years ago, Neha was 3 times as old as her brother. Now the sum of their ages is 30. How old is Neha now?
quiz.mistake: Uses present ages in the 'five years ago' clue

quiz.q: A wallet has ₹10 and ₹50 notes, 16 notes in all, worth ₹400. How many ₹50 notes?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which note is which

quiz.q: The digits of a two-digit number add to 11. Reversing the digits makes it 45 more. What is the number?
quiz.mistake: Gives the reversed number

quiz.q: The incomes of A and B are in ratio 5 : 4 and their spending in ratio 7 : 5. Each saves ₹3000. What is A's income?
quiz.explain: 5k − 7m = 3000 and 4k − 5m = 3000. Subtracting gives k = 2m; so 3m = 3000, m = 1000, k = 2000.
quiz.mistake: Uses the same multiplier for income and spending

quiz.q: 3 chairs and 2 tables cost ₹4300; 2 chairs and 3 tables cost ₹4700. What does one table cost?
quiz.explain: Add: 5(c + t) = 9000, so c + t = 1800. Subtract: t − c = 400. So t = 1100.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the equations only

quiz.q: A taxi charges a fixed amount plus a rate per km. 10 km costs ₹150 and 15 km costs ₹200. What is the fixed charge?
quiz.mistake: Gives the rate instead

quiz.q: A fraction x/y: if 2 is added to both parts it becomes 2/3, and if 3 is subtracted from both it becomes 1/2. What is the fraction?
quiz.mistake: Gives one of the reduced fractions

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I solve a problem with two unknown numbers?"
teach.praise: Wonderful! Name both unknowns, write an equation for each clue, solve and check!
teach.nudge: How many equations do you need for two unknowns? How do you make sure the answer fits?

learn.hook: Over 1100 years ago, Mahaviracharya asked: what is the price of one citron and one wood-apple? Pairs of equations are that old!
points: Mahaviracharya (9th century) posed: 9 citrons and 7 wood-apples cost 107; 7 citrons and 9 wood-apples cost 101. Adding: 16(x + y) = 208, so x + y = 13; subtracting: 2(x − y) = 6, so x − y = 3. Citron 8, wood-apple 5.
Babylonian tablets, the Chinese 'Nine Chapters' (with a method like elimination) and Indian texts all solved such problems long ago.
Graphical method for word problems: write both equations, draw both lines carefully on graph paper, and read the meeting point. Then check it in both equations.
Comparing plans: two phone plans y = 200 + 2x and y = 50 + 5x meet where 200 + 2x = 50 + 5x, at x = 50. Below 50 units the second is cheaper; above 50, the first.

example.q: Gym Plan A costs ₹500 to join plus ₹300 a month; Plan B costs ₹1100 to join plus ₹200 a month. After how many months do they cost the same?

learn.reallife: Before buying a two-wheeler or a phone plan, families compare costs over time, exactly like reading where two lines meet.

games.title: Methods through history
items: Mahaviracharya posed a famous citron and wood-apple problem.
It appears in his Ganita Sara Sangraha.
The Chinese 'Nine Chapters' solved pairs with a method like elimination.
It arranged coefficients in tables and combined rows.
Reading a graph can give only approximate answers if the meeting point is not on grid lines.
If two cost lines never meet, the plans always cost the same.
Parallel lines mean one plan is always cheaper.
The meeting point of two lines satisfies both equations.

quiz.q: In Mahaviracharya's problem, 9x + 7y = 107 and 7x + 9y = 101. Adding gives 16x + 16y = 208. What is x + y?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 16

quiz.q: Subtracting the equations gives 2x − 2y = 6. With x + y = 13, what is the price of a citron (x)?
quiz.explain: x − y = 3 and x + y = 13 give 2x = 16.
quiz.mistake: Gives the wood-apple's price

quiz.q: Which ancient text from China solved pairs of equations with a method like elimination?
options: The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art
quiz.explain: Its 'fangcheng' method combined rows of coefficients.
quiz.mistake: Picks an Indian or Greek text

quiz.q: Plan P: ₹200 fixed + ₹2 per unit. Plan Q: ₹50 fixed + ₹5 per unit. At how many units do they cost the same?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the rates the wrong way

quiz.q: For 80 units, which plan (P or Q above) is cheaper?
quiz.mistake: Picks the plan with the smaller fixed charge

quiz.q: Two lines drawn on graph paper meet at (4, 3). What should you do next?
quiz.explain: Graph readings can be slightly off; substituting confirms the answer.
quiz.mistake: Trusts the drawing without checking

quiz.q: Riya walks at 4 km/h starting at 0 km; Arjun cycles at 12 km/h starting 2 hours later from the same place. Using d = 4t and d = 12(t − 2), when does Arjun catch up?
quiz.explain: 4t = 12t − 24 gives 8t = 24.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the 2-hour delay

quiz.q: Two cost lines for plans are parallel. What does this mean?
options: They cost the same at some point
One plan is always cheaper by the same amount
quiz.explain: Parallel lines never meet, so the gap between costs never changes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all lines meet somewhere

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How can a graph help me choose between two phone plans?"
teach.praise: Smart! Draw both cost lines; where they meet the plans cost the same, and on each side one is cheaper!
teach.nudge: What does the meeting point of the lines tell you? What about before and after it?
